attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter essay, endorsed.

semantics.note: Keeps the hedge ('appears') and the exceptions (NVIDIA, Dell, Supermicro). 'Nobody in AI' is a bit broader than the source, which is about GPU buyers and operators, but it is close enough.

contract.note: 'Seems' marks this as an impression, and 'make any money' has no measure or scope. Any test would need a measure he did not supply, so leaving it unscored is fair.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged impression ('nobody seems to make any money') with no measure of profit and no clear scope for 'nobody'. Hyperscalers do not break out AI profit. The packet cites no outcome evidence, and the CoreWeave release cuts both ways depending on the measure. It cannot be scored without adding precision he did not give.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, endorsed.

semantics.note: Captures the core claim (floundering, negative gross margins, excluding OpenAI and Anthropic). It drops the 'several-hundred million dollar bursts' element, but the contract restores it. This is a generalisation about AI startups as a group.

contract.note: The plain reading (a group generalisation over Jul–Sep 2025, in three parts) is ordinary and fair. 'Floundering' has no threshold, so judgement is needed.

evidence.note: August 2025 report that AI coding startups, Windsurf in particular, had 'very negative' gross margins and that Windsurf sold itself. Supports the margin part for a key segment. Anonymous source.
Replit's $250M round and Cognition's $400M+ round in September 2025 support the funding-burst part. Note that the rounds came at rising valuations.
Replit's valuation nearly tripled and its revenue (as the company stated it) grew from $2.8M to $150M annualised. That does not fit 'struggling to stay alive' for a leading startup.

Published Nov 2025, before the evaluation date. Gamma's self-reported profitability over two years covers the period. A company disclosure about a single firm, and the event_date label looks imprecise.
The Replit CEO's October 2025 claim that the company is gross-margin positive while 'many' rivals are not. Self-reported and after the period, so context only.

reviews.rationale: The funding-burst part holds (Replit $250M, Cognition $400M+). Negative gross margins are supported for AI coding startups such as Windsurf. But the 'floundering, struggling to stay alive' generalisation is not borne out for the leading startups in the packet: Replit and Cognition were raising at sharply higher valuations with fast revenue growth, and Gamma reports profitability. The evidence is anecdotal on both sides.
